div.head: As Alm Prol.
div.ab: Ego Æþelstanus rex notifico omnibus prepositis meis in regno meo, quod, consilio Wulfhelmes archiepiscopi mei et omnium episcoporum meorum et Dei ministrorum, ad remissionem peccatorum meorum et adquisitionem uitę ęternç uolo, ut pascatis omni uia pauperem unum Anglicum indigentem, si sit ibi, uel alium inueniatis.

Ic Æþelstane cyning eallum minum gerefum binnon mine rice gecyþe, mid geþeahte Wulfhelmes mines ærcebisceopes ⁊ ealra mina oþra bisceopa ⁊ Godes ðeowa, for mina sinna forgyfenesse, þæt ic wille, þæt ge fedaþ ealle wæga án earm Engliscmon, gif ge him habbaþ, oþþe oþerne gefindaþ.

Ic, Æþelstane cyning, eallum minum gerefum binnon mine rice gecyþe, mid geþeahte Wulfhelmes mines ærcebisceopes ⁊ ealre mina oþra bisceopa ⁊ Godes ðeowa, for mina sinna forgyfenesse, þæt ic wille, þæt ge fedaþ ealle wæga án earm Engliscmon, gif ge him habbaþ, oþþe oþerne gefindaþ.

I, King Ethelstan, with the advice of Wulfhelm, my archbishop, and of all my other bishops and ecclesiastics, for the forgiveness of my sins, make known to all my reeves within my kingdom, that it is my wish that you shall always provide a destitute Englishman with food, if you have such an one [in your district], or if you find one [elsewhere].

Ich, König Aethelstan, verkünde allen meinen Vögten innerhalb meines Reiches, mit Beirath Wulfhelms, meines Erzbischofs, und aller meiner anderen Bischöfe und Gottesdiener, zur Vergebung meiner Sünden (und Erlangung des ewigen Lebens Quadr.), dass ich will, dass ihr immer Einen armen Engländer beköstigt, wenn ihr einen solchen [in eurem Bezirk] habt, oder [dass ihr] einen anderen [anderswo] auffindet.

I, King Æthelstan, make known to all my reeves within my kingdom, with the counsel of Wulfhelm, my archbishop, and of all my other bishops and servants of God, for the forgiveness of my sins (and the attainment of eternal life, Quadr.), that I will that you always feed one poor Englishman, if you have such a one [in your district], or [that you] find another [elsewhere].
div.note: Column The Latin is the Quadripartitus (Liebermann's right-hand column), corrected against Gesetze I p. 148. The Old English survives only in Lambarde's Archaionomia (1568), f. 57v (Ld), now in column N. Liebermann compares I As Prol.
